newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH UNION AKAVA CALLS FOR NEW INCOME TAX CUTS.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH UNION AKAVA CALLS FOR NEW INCOME TAX CUTS.

text.p: The central union for academic professionals in Finland (Akava) said in a statement on Tuesday that the government should make further cuts in wage earners' income taxes in 1998.
"The most efficient way to increase domestic demand is to lower wage earners' income taxes," Akava's executive board said.

"In next year's budget, the government should bravely lower wage earners' income taxes in all income brackets," Akava said, referring to government talks late in February on the 1998-99 state budget frames.
In economic policy, the focus next year should be squarely on increasing domestic demand and on retaining the competitiveness of exports, the academics' union said.
